title: Recall Quiz: Later Victorians: Dickens, Hardy, Eliot, Arnold

questions.q: The fictional region of 'Wessex' serves as the setting for the novels of which Victorian author?
questions.explanation: Hardy based Wessex on the real counties of southwestern England.

questions.q: What was the real name of the author who wrote under the pseudonym George Eliot?
questions.explanation: Mary Ann Evans used a male pen name to ensure her work was judged seriously.

questions.q: Which novel by Charles Dickens begins with the famous line 'It was the best of times, it was the worst of times'?
questions.explanation: This is the opening of his historical novel set during the French Revolution.

questions.q: Thomas Hardy's novels are primarily characterized by a philosophy of:
questions.explanation: Hardy's characters are often victims of blind, uncaring fate and strict social conventions.

questions.q: Which poem by Matthew Arnold famously laments the 'melancholy, long, withdrawing roar' of the Sea of Faith?
questions.explanation: Dover Beach is the ultimate expression of Victorian anxiety over the loss of religion.

questions.q: Which novel by George Eliot is subtitled 'A Study of Provincial Life' and is widely considered her masterpiece?
questions.explanation: Middlemarch explores a vast web of interconnected lives in a provincial English town.

questions.q: The public outrage against the bleakness and anti-religious themes of which novel caused Thomas Hardy to stop writing fiction entirely?
questions.explanation: The harsh reception of Jude the Obscure led Hardy to focus only on poetry for the rest of his life.

questions.q: Pip, Miss Havisham, and the convict Magwitch are characters from which Dickens novel?
questions.explanation: These are the central characters in the masterpiece 'Great Expectations'.
